smells.finding: All derivation/assembly/persistence logic is concentrated in derive.py; scripts/derive_segment_maps.py contains only argument parsing and a per-weekend loop, with zero duplicated business logic (confirmed by reading -- the CLI calls derive_segment_map/write_segment_map directly for every decision).
derive.py changes for exactly one reason class -- composition/persistence of a weekend's SegmentMap; no unrelated concerns (e.g. CLI argument shape, DB schema) are folded into the same functions.
Attribute access is one level deep throughout (base_tiling.boundaries_m, vocabulary.class_ids, ref.lap_length_m) -- no a.b.c.d chains.
No unused hooks, no abstract base classes, no config knob without a caller; every parameter on derive_segment_map is exercised by either the test suite or the CLI.

The dense module/function docstrings explain WHY (the geometry-only-hash load-bearing property, the map_version global-uniqueness tension) not confusing code needing an apology -- consistent with identity.py/runtime.py's own already-dense docstring convention in this package.
